name: customers/C02gxaaci/policySchemas/chrome.devices.managedguest.BeforeunloadEventCancelByPreventDefaultEnabled
policyDescription: Behavior of event.preventDefault() for beforeunload event.

fieldDescriptions.description: This policy allows to control whether confirmation dialog is shown when a page calls preventDefault for beforeunload event. Historically, Google Chrome didn't show these dialogs, but the default behavior is being changed. This policy is a temporary escape hatch, meant for the enterprises whose websites got broken because of the new behavior and that need some time before they get fixed. If this policy is enabled, then the cancel confirmation dialog is shown when a page calls preventDefault for beforeunload event. If this policy is disabled, then no cancel confirmation dialog is shown when a page calls preventDefault for beforeunload event. If this policy is not set, the default behavior will be used, according to Google Chrome feature rollout plan.

name: customers/C02gxaaci/policySchemas/chrome.devices.managedguest.LacrosAvailability
policyDescription: Configuration of Chrome browser as an independent app.

fieldDescriptions.description: ChromeOS is making an architecture change to make Chrome browser an independent app which is decoupled from the ChromeOS window manager and system UI. This new architecture will become the default in 2024 in the “Migration” phase, and then the only available option as part of the “Final Phase”. See the help documentation for more details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ma6hU-p7hfobl7Drp3_F9x6TcHU-KxckS0muWp6W8-Q/edit?resourcekey=0-dvGsW0DW19Kj8NOfrauCGw#heading=h.ttjg5n78pk3. Note - exact dates are subject to change as we receive feedback from users. It is highly recommended that you test critical workflows by enabling this setting for a cohort of your users. Please file feedback with Google Support. Please see the support article for more details including the latest timing for the various stages of rollout and best practices for testing.
